g.text: What it shows: the same chips on llama2-70b-99 across all three serving scenarios. Offline batches everything; server

g.text: holds a latency target under a Poisson arrival pattern; interactive tightens that target further. 8 chips submitted all

g.text: Note: The gap between the bars is the price of responsiveness, and it is the reason an offline figure must never be quoted as serving

g.text: capacity: it assumes every request is already waiting. Interactive costs 15% to 79% of offline throughput across these chips. Every

g.text: figure is a vendor-tuned submission to the closed division, where the model and the accuracy target are fixed and the system is

g.text: optimised hard for the benchmark. Production serving runs below this, so these are ceilings rather than expected throughput.
